title: Investigative Researcher Roadmap
summary: Develop the research, verification, data analysis and reporting skills needed to investigate complex public-interest questions, trace evidence, analyse records and support accurate investigative journalism.

facts.Current degree: BJMC / B.A. Journalism & Mass Communication – Data Journalism / Fact-Checking
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a three-year bachelor's degree with an optional fourth-year honours route if offered by your university. The career horizons extend from 2026 to 2046.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: A portfolio of documented investigations, source trails, public-records research and data-backed reports.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Expertise in areas such as public finance, corporate accountability, politics, environmental reporting or digital investigations.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Senior investigative research, investigations editing, team leadership or specialist research management.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Leadership in investigative projects, advanced verification methods and responsible, evidence-based research.

blocks.text: The goal is to establish a repeatable research process: define a question, find reliable records, verify sources, analyse evidence, document uncertainty and present findings clearly.

rows.text: A research brief on a public-interest question.
A 500–800-word brief with at least five relevant sources.
A public-records and official-document research project.
A source register, document archive and evidence summary.
One report with primary-source links and a transparent methodology.
A spreadsheet investigation using a public dataset.
A cleaned dataset, documented calculations and a clear finding.
A case study involving multiple sources and a timeline of events.
A sourced timeline, interview notes and a written report.
An editor-reviewed research memo or approved published work.
A deeper investigation in a chosen subject area.
A research plan, source map, evidence log and interim findings.
A final investigation with reproducible supporting analysis.
A publishable report, methodology note and organised supporting records where lawful.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If your university offers a four-year honours programme, use the additional year for a substantial investigation, research dissertation or data-driven public-interest project. Verify your institution's current programme structure and eligibility.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Move from collecting information to designing investigations, managing research teams and assessing evidence quality. Learn computational research and AI-assisted document analysis while independently verifying outputs. Maintain strong standards for privacy, source protection, lawful access, right of reply and correction of errors.

Career progression

blocks.label: Year 1–2
blocks.text: Student Researcher / Research Intern

blocks.label: Year 3–5
blocks.text: Investigative Research Assistant / Junior Researcher

blocks.label: Year 5–9
blocks.text: Investigative Researcher / Senior Researcher

blocks.label: Year 9–14
blocks.text: Investigations Editor / Research Lead

blocks.label: Year 14+
blocks.text: Investigations Director / Research Director / Independent Investigator

These milestones are illustrative, not fixed promotion timelines. Some researchers move into specialist analysis or policy work; others lead investigative teams or establish independent research practices.
PhD routes
A PhD is optional for professional investigative research. It may be useful for academic work, advanced policy research or developing new research methods.

Check each institution's accepted qualifications, entrance requirements, supervisor availability and funding rules.

2040–2046: remain relevant. Build expertise in complex investigations, research management, data interpretation and responsible digital investigation. Learn how to use AI-assisted document analysis without treating machine-generated findings as established evidence. Long-term credibility depends on transparent methods, source protection, lawful research, fair treatment of subjects and the ability to explain what the evidence does—and does not—show.
